docs.title: kcp report plan
docs.text: Generate a Migration Plan to migrate to Confluent Cloud

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
Generate a Migration Plan to migrate to Confluent Cloud from a kcp state file produced by kcp scan or kcp discover, or from your answers alone with no state file.

For each scanned cluster the plan recommends a target cluster type, sizing, networking, authentication, and data-migration approach, and lists the questions a scan can't answer.

How it works: kcp auto-answers everything it can from the scan. What it can't derive is written to plan-inputs.yaml (in the current directory) — fleet-wide questions once under all_clusters:, per-cluster facts under each cluster, each answer a short, stable token with the full wording in the comment above it. Edit that file in place and re-run; kcp reads your answers back, folds them into the plan, and rewrites the file with any follow-ups revealed — so it converges over a couple of passes.

Output: plan.md and plan.json go to --output-dir (default ./plan-output); plan-inputs.yaml is read from and written back to --plan-inputs (default ./plan-inputs.yaml) — edit it in place between runs.

kcp report plan [flags]

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# First pass: state file in; writes ./plan-inputs.yaml + plan.md/plan.json
  kcp report plan --state-file kcp-state.json

  # Edit ./plan-inputs.yaml, then re-run — same command refines the plan
  kcp report plan --state-file kcp-state.json

  # JSON only
  kcp report plan --state-file kcp-state.json --output json

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
--cluster-id string    [Optional] Plan only this cluster (name or ARN). Default: every cluster in the scan.
  -h, --help                 help for plan

docs.title: kcp scan clusters
docs.text: Scan Kafka clusters using the Kafka Admin API

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
Scan MSK or Apache Kafka clusters — including Confluent Platform and other Kafka-API-compatible distributions — to discover topics, ACLs, and other metadata via the Kafka Admin API. Results are merged into the kcp-state.json file.

Source-specific notes:

  • --source-type msk reads cluster connection details from the msk-credentials.yaml file produced by kcp discover. Enable exactly one authentication method per cluster in that file before scanning. SCRAM is forced to SHA-512 (the only mechanism MSK supports).
  • --source-type apache-kafka reads from a hand-authored apache-kafka-credentials.yaml file. SASL/SCRAM defaults to SHA-256 — set auth_method.sasl_scram.mechanism: SHA512 if your cluster requires SHA-512. The full schema and worked examples are documented at Apache Kafka configuration → Credentials.

For the step-by-step workflow from discovery to viewing the results, see Getting started.

Consumer groups:

  • Consumer group discovery runs by default; pass --skip-consumer-groups to turn it off. For every group KCP records its KIP-848 type (classic, consumer, share, streams), state, and coordinator, and merges them into the state file.
  • Reading the group type requires a broker running Kafka 3.8 or newer; against older brokers the type is reported as blank and every group is treated as classic-protocol.
  • Only classic groups are fully described (members and their assigned topics). consumer, share, and streams groups record type, state, and coordinator but not member-level detail (that needs the newer ConsumerGroupDescribe API); they are flagged with incomplete detail in the state file and UI.

Metrics collection (Apache Kafka only):

  • --metrics jolokia polls each broker's Jolokia HTTP endpoint live for the duration set by --metrics-duration (interval: --metrics-interval, default 10s).
  • --metrics prometheus queries a Prometheus server for historical metrics over --metrics-range (e.g. 7d, 30d).

Both backends produce the same metric shape and feed reports and the UI. See Apache Kafka configuration → Metrics collection for the metric list, the counter-based rate calculation, and authentication options.

kcp scan clusters [flags]

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Scan an MSK cluster (credentials from kcp discover)
  kcp scan clusters --source-type msk --state-file kcp-state.json --credentials-file msk-credentials.yaml

  # Scan an Apache Kafka cluster (hand-authored credentials)
  kcp scan clusters --source-type apache-kafka --state-file kcp-state.json --credentials-file apache-kafka-credentials.yaml

  # Apache Kafka with live Jolokia metric collection
  kcp scan clusters --source-type apache-kafka --state-file kcp-state.json \
      --credentials-file apache-kafka-credentials.yaml \
      --metrics jolokia --metrics-duration 5m --metrics-interval 10s

  # Apache Kafka with historical Prometheus metrics
  kcp scan clusters --source-type apache-kafka --state-file kcp-state.json \
      --credentials-file apache-kafka-credentials.yaml \
      --metrics prometheus --metrics-range 30d

docs.title: Migration assets
docs.text:
This folder is scoped to one manifest: migration.yaml (kind: Migration), which drives the kcp migration resources direct-API commands (validate, create) — keep any future addition here scoped to that manifest, not the unrelated one below.

kcp migration cutover execute|lag-check is driven by a different manifest, gateway-static-migration.yaml (kind: GatewayMigration; there is one example per migration type), which shares this one's apiVersion and parser but nothing else. Its docs live outside this folder, published normally: see migration manifest reference and gateway-examples/gateway-static-migration.yaml. A file written for one kind is rejected with a clear error if pointed at the other command.

A kcp migration resources migration is driven by a single manifest (migration.yaml) that describes the desired end state, plus external credential files that hold auth only. This section provides a ready-to-copy reference manifest, worked examples for each scenario, and a catalog of every credential format.

manifest reference field-by-field reference for every manifest section — the single source of truth for field detail migration.example.yaml the fully-annotated reference manifest — every field, with comments examples/ minimal, validated manifests per scenario (below) credentials/ one credential file per auth method, with a slot-applicability table

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Example Topics mode Cluster link Source → target new-topics new none Apache Kafka → Confluent Cloud mirror-topics mirror destination-initiated MSK → Confluent Cloud source-initiated mirror source-initiated private Confluent Platform → Confluent Cloud acls-native — none Apache Kafka → Confluent Cloud — native ACLs only acls-iam-explicit — none MSK → Confluent Cloud — IAM plane, explicit named roles acls-iam-discover — none MSK → Confluent Cloud — IAM plane, auto-discovered roles acls-native-and-iam — none MSK → Confluent Cloud — native + IAM union, explicit service-account mapping

Validate, preview, then create any of them:

kcp migration resources validate -f migration.yaml
kcp migration resources create -f migration.yaml --dry-run   # preview; changes nothing
kcp migration resources create -f migration.yaml

create is additive: it only creates what is absent and reports — never alters or deletes — what already exists. --dry-run prints the same plan without making any change.

docs.title: Manifest at a glance
docs.text:
The manifest carries all addresses; credentials: fields reference external files that carry secrets only. Each connection is a uniform {address, credentials} pair:

  • Kafka slots (spec.source, spec.clusterLink.source, spec.clusterLink.destination) — bootstrapServers + credentials.
  • REST slots (spec.target + spec.target.kafka.restEndpoint, spec.clusterLink.sourceRest) — endpoint/restEndpoint + credentials. On spec.target this Kafka cluster / REST-v3 credential is clusterCredentials (cluster link, topics, ACLs); a Confluent Cloud target also takes cloudCredentials — a distinct Cloud/Global API key — whenever spec.acls is present (to provision service accounts and reconcile ACL principals via IAM v2).

Which credential family each slot uses, and every supported auth method, is in the credential catalog.

docs.title: Manifest sections
docs.text: spec.source and spec.target are always required; spec.clusterLink, spec.topics, spec.serviceAccounts, and spec.acls are opt-in and correspond to independently reconciled units of work. Every field — types, defaults, required/forbidden rules, and behaviour — is documented in the manifest reference.

docs.title: Editor support
docs.text:
migration.example.yaml and every example carry a # yaml-language-server: $schema=… modeline, so VS Code with the Red Hat YAML extension gives autocomplete and inline validation automatically. For offline/repo-local use, map the schema in your workspace settings instead:

// .vscode/settings.json
"yaml.schemas": {
  "internal/manifest/migration.schema.json": ["migration*.yaml"]
}

docs.title: Manifest reference
docs.text:
kcp migration resources create -f migration.yaml migrates a Kafka source — AWS MSK, Apache Kafka®, or Confluent Platform — to a Confluent target (Confluent Cloud or Confluent Platform) by declaring the desired end state in a single YAML manifest. This page is the field-by-field reference for that manifest.

For an annotated, ready-to-copy manifest see migration.example.yaml; for worked per-scenario manifests see examples/; for the credential file formats each credentials: slot points at, see the credential catalog.

docs.title: Execution model
docs.text:
The manifest is declarative: you describe the cluster link, topics, service accounts, and ACLs you want on the target, and create reconciles the target toward that state.

  • Additive-only. Reconcilers only ever create resources or confirm they are already present. Nothing on the target is deleted, altered, or pruned.
  • Idempotent. Re-running create against an unchanged source and manifest reports every resource as already present and makes no further change.
  • Reads the source live. The source is connected to and read at run time from spec.source.bootstrapServers plus its credentials file. Topic lists, topic configs, and ACLs always reflect the source's current state at the moment of the run — no intermediate state file is consulted.
  • --dry-run. Preconditions and planning still run — live connections to source and target are opened and real state is read — but no mutation is performed. Output is rendered in future tense ("Planned") rather than past tense ("Applying"). Use it to review exactly what create would do without --dry-run.
  • Drift reporting. For the cluster link, mirror topics, and new topics, an existing resource that differs from what the manifest describes is reported as drift. Drift is report-only; existing target state is never overwritten.

Validation runs structurally first, with no I/O; any error aborts the run before the source or target is touched. At least one of spec.clusterLink, spec.topics, or spec.acls must be present, or the run refuses with "nothing to create".

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
apiVersion: kcp.confluent.io/v1alpha1   # required, exact literal
kind: Migration                          # required, exact literal
metadata:
  name: my-migration                     # required, non-blank
spec:
  source:          { ... }               # required — cluster to migrate from
  target:          { ... }               # required — cluster to migrate to
  clusterLink:     { ... }               # optional — cluster link config
  topics:          { ... }               # optional — mirror or new topics
  serviceAccounts: { ... }               # optional — Confluent Cloud identity resolution
  acls:            { ... }               # optional — ACL migration (Confluent Cloud target)

apiVersion must equal kcp.confluent.io/v1alpha1 and kind must equal Migration, exactly. metadata.name is required and non-blank; it identifies the migration and is not otherwise constrained. spec.source and spec.target are always required; the remaining spec sections are opt-in and correspond to independently reconciled units of work.

docs.title: spec.source
docs.text:
The cluster being migrated from, read live at run time.

Field Type Required Notes type enum yes msk, apache-kafka, or confluent-platform. bootstrapServers []string yes Non-empty; each entry host:port with a numeric port 1-65535. credentials string (path) yes Kafka credentials file (Kafka family).

type gates several capabilities elsewhere in the manifest: IAM source authentication and spec.acls.iam are legal only for msk; SCRAM against MSK must resolve to SCRAM-SHA-512; and spec.clusterLink.mode: source is legal only for a confluent-platform or confluent-cloud source.

bootstrapServers is the sole source of the source addresses — they always come from the manifest, never from a credentials file. The credentials file here is used only to read the source cluster id; the cluster link's own source connection (in destination mode) carries its own separate credentials.

docs.title: spec.target
docs.text:
The cluster being migrated to. Required fields depend on type.

Field Type Required Notes type enum yes confluent-cloud or confluent-platform. kafka.restEndpoint string yes REST v3 endpoint for cluster-link, topic, and ACL operations. clusterCredentials string (path) yes REST credentials for the /kafka/v3 surface (REST family). clusterId string Confluent Cloud only Required for confluent-cloud; forbidden for confluent-platform. cloudCredentials string (path) conditional Confluent Cloud only; required whenever spec.acls is present (REST family).

For confluent-cloud, clusterId is required and is used directly for link and REST operations. For confluent-platform, the cluster id is discovered live from the REST endpoint on first use, so clusterId must not be set.

cloudCredentials is a Confluent Cloud Cloud/Global API key. It is valid only for a confluent-cloud target, and is required whenever spec.acls is present: it is used both to provision service accounts (Confluent Cloud IAM v2 rejects a Kafka-cluster API key) and, regardless of spec.serviceAccounts.autoCreate, to build the numeric-id → sa--id map the ACL reconciler needs for idempotent re-runs.

docs.title: spec.clusterLink
docs.text:
Optional. Required when spec.topics.mode: mirror. Configures a cluster link between source and target.

Field Type Required Default Notes name string yes — Link name. In source mode, shared by both link objects. mode enum no destination destination or source. source object destination mode — bootstrapServers[] + credentials. Link → source connection. sourceRest object source mode — endpoint + credentials (REST family). destination object source mode — bootstrapServers[] + credentials. Source-side link → destination connection. prefix string no "" Prepended to mirror topic names; immutable once the link exists. consumerOffsetSync object no enabled See below. topicConfigSync.intervalMs int no 0 >= 0; 0 = server default; written only when > 0. configs map[string]string no — Free-form additional link configs; see below.

docs.title: Modes
docs.text:
• destination (default) — one link object, created on the destination (target), pulling from the source. Requires spec.clusterLink.source; sourceRest and destination must not be set. The destination dials the source, so the source must be reachable from the destination.
  • source — two link objects sharing one name: a destination-side object created first, then a source-side object created on the source's own REST surface, which initiates the link outbound to the destination. Requires sourceRest and destination; source must not be set. Legal only when spec.source.type is confluent-platform or confluent-cloud, since the source must expose a REST surface to host the source-side object — msk and apache-kafka sources cannot initiate a link.

bidirectional is explicitly rejected: it describes DR / active-active, not a migration; use two unidirectional links instead.

docs.title: prefix
docs.text: When set, mirror topic names become prefix + sourceName. It maps to the link config cluster.link.prefix and is immutable once the link exists. Set it through this field only; the read-only derived key link.prefix is rejected if placed in configs.

docs.title: consumerOffsetSync
docs.text:
Field Type Default Notes enable *bool true True even when the whole consumerOffsetSync block is omitted. intervalMs int 0 >= 0; 0 = server default (consumer.offset.sync.ms); written only when > 0. groupFilters []filter include-all See below.

Omitting consumerOffsetSync entirely still enables offset sync for all consumer groups: when sync is enabled and no filters are given, the default is a single include-all filter (name: "*", patternType: LITERAL, filterType: INCLUDE). Each groupFilters entry has name, patternType (LITERAL or PREFIXED), and filterType (INCLUDE or EXCLUDE).

docs.title: configs
docs.text: An escape hatch for arbitrary link configs as a string → string map, merged with the configs derived from the typed fields above. Keys owned by a typed field are rejected so the merge can never conflict: cluster.link.prefix, consumer.offset.sync.enable, consumer.offset.sync.ms, consumer.offset.group.filters, topic.config.sync.ms, and the read-only link.prefix alias (use prefix instead).

docs.title: spec.topics
docs.text:
Optional. Selects source topics and reproduces them on the target.

Field Type Required Notes mode enum yes mirror or new. include []string yes Non-empty; each a path.Match glob. exclude []string no Glob-validated; exclude always wins over include.

docs.title: Modes
docs.text:
• mirror — creates a read-only mirror topic per selected source topic via the cluster link, so spec.clusterLink.name must be set. Mirror names are the link's live cluster.link.prefix + source topic name (falling back to the manifest's clusterLink.prefix before the link is readable). An existing mirror is Present; a target name already taken — by a plain topic, or by a mirror on a different link — is reported as drift and skipped.
  • new — creates a plain topic per selected source topic; no cluster link needed. Partition count and every explicitly-set (non-default) source topic config are reproduced. Topics are created at the target's default replication factor (Confluent Cloud uses RF=3). An existing target topic whose partition count differs from the source is reported as drift and left untouched.

docs.title: Selection
docs.text: A topic is selected if it matches at least one include glob and no exclude glob. Internal topics — names starting with _, e.g. __consumer_offsets, _schemas, _confluent-* — are excluded by default even under a broad * include; they are included only when an include pattern that itself starts with _ matches them (e.g. _foo or _*). The result is deduplicated and sorted.

docs.title: spec.serviceAccounts
docs.text:
Optional; valid only for a confluent-cloud target. Resolves each ACL principal to a target identity before ACLs are written.

Field Type Default Notes autoCreate bool false Find-or-create a Confluent Cloud service account per unmapped principal. mapping map[string]string — Explicit source principal → target id.

An explicit mapping entry always wins over autoCreate. Mapping values must be a sa-, u-, or pool- id, optionally User:-prefixed. sa- and u- ids are checked for existence; a pool- id is accepted with a not-verified warning (identity pools cannot be looked up by id). An empty mapping value is treated as no mapping and falls through to autoCreate.

When autoCreate is true, a service account is derived and find-or-created for every principal without a mapping entry. An existing account found by name whose description does not record the expected source principal is a hard error (naming collision). The special principals User:* and User:ANONYMOUS are skipped, with a warning, unless explicitly mapped.

With autoCreate off and a principal left unmapped, create stops with an error listing every unresolved principal.

docs.title: spec.acls
docs.text:
Optional; valid only for a confluent-cloud target. Migrates ACLs read from the source, optionally unioned with grants derived from the AWS MSK IAM authorization plane.

Field Type Required Notes include []string yes Non-empty; glob matched against an ACL's principal or resource name. exclude []string no Glob-validated; exclude always wins. iam object no AWS MSK IAM authorization plane; see below.

include/exclude globs match either the ACL's principal or its resource name (not resource type or operation). When spec.acls is present, the target's cloudCredentials is required (see spec.target).

docs.title: spec.acls.iam
docs.text:
Valid only when spec.source.type: msk.

Field Type Required Notes clusterArn string yes Well-formed MSK cluster ARN; scopes discovered grants to this cluster. principalArns []string one of the two Named IAM role/user ARNs to translate. discoverAllRoles bool one of the two Enumerate every workload IAM role in the account. verifyEffectiveAccess bool no Default false; see below.

clusterArn must be a fully-populated MSK cluster ARN (arn:aws:kafka:<region>:<account>:cluster/<name>/<uuid>); it scopes discovered grants by matching the cluster name and UUID.

principalArns and discoverAllRoles are mutually exclusive, and exactly one is required when the iam block is present. Each principalArns entry must be a well-formed IAM role or user ARN (arn:aws:iam::<account>:role|user/<name>); STS assumed-role ARNs are normalized to their underlying role ARN. discoverAllRoles enumerates every IAM role in the account, excluding AWS service-linked and SSO-provisioned roles.

verifyEffectiveAccess, when true, simulates each principal's identity-based policies and its attached permissions boundary via iam:SimulatePrincipalPolicy, and migrates only the grants that are effectively allowed.

docs.title: ACL pipeline
docs.text: The ACL reconciler runs a fixed pipeline: read the native source ACLs; optionally gather and translate IAM-derived ACLs (applying the effective-access filter first when verifyEffectiveAccess is set); union the two planes; filter by include/exclude; normalize for Confluent Cloud (drop CC-invalid operations, normalize hosts to *, collapse redundant Describe/DescribeConfigs grants); deduplicate on the exact ACL tuple; resolve each distinct principal to a target identity, provisioning service accounts as needed; and write the ACLs.

docs.title: Credential files
docs.text:
The manifest holds no secrets. Every credentials: slot points at an external YAML file that carries auth only; addresses (bootstrapServers, REST endpoint) stay in the manifest. Two credential families exist, one per endpoint kind, each with the auth method selected by the presence of exactly one block and decoded strictly (unknown or duplicate keys are rejected):

  • Kafka family — spec.source.credentials, spec.clusterLink.source.credentials, spec.clusterLink.destination.credentials.
  • REST family — spec.target.clusterCredentials, spec.target.cloudCredentials, spec.clusterLink.sourceRest.credentials.

Which slot uses which family, and every supported auth method with a copy-ready file per method, is documented in the credential catalog.

docs.title: Dependencies and ordering
docs.text:
Reconcilers run in two independent tracks. Tracks run independently — a failure in one never skips the other — but within a track execution is fail-fast.

  • Track A: clusterLink → topics. The cluster link is created and verified first because mirror topics depend on it.
  • Track B: serviceAccounts → acls. Service accounts resolve to identities before ACLs are written with the correct target principals.

Transient races are retried narrowly (up to 30s): the source-side link create in source mode against a not-yet-propagated destination object, and mirror-topic creates against a not-yet-resolvable link. All other errors are reported per item.

docs.title: Credential file catalog
docs.text:
A migration manifest holds no secrets. Every connection in the manifest is an {address, credentials} pair: the address (bootstrapServers / REST endpoint) lives in the manifest, and credentials: points at an external file that holds auth only. This folder is a catalog of every supported credential file — one per auth method — that you can copy next to your manifest and point a slot at.

There are two credential families, matched to the kind of endpoint a slot talks to.

docs.title: Which family does a slot use?
docs.text: Manifest slot Mode Talks to Family spec.source.credentials both source Kafka (reads the cluster id) Kafka spec.clusterLink.source.credentials destination the link → source Kafka Kafka spec.clusterLink.destination.credentials source the source-side link → destination Kafka Kafka spec.target.clusterCredentials both target Kafka Admin REST (/kafka/v3: cluster link, topics, ACLs) REST spec.target.cloudCredentials both Confluent Cloud Cloud/Global API — required when spec.acls is present (CC only) REST spec.clusterLink.sourceRest.credentials source the source's Admin REST (creates the outbound link) REST

docs.title: Kafka credentials
docs.text:
Auth-only, single-cluster. Specify exactly one method block — its presence selects it (no auth_method: wrapper, no use: flag). An optional top-level insecure_skip_tls_verify: false applies to test environments only.

File Method Notes kafka-iam.yaml iam MSK source read only; CC can't present IAM (links to MSK use SCRAM) kafka-sasl-scram.yaml sasl_scram always TLS (SASL_SSL); mechanism required (SHA256/SHA512) kafka-sasl-plain.yaml sasl_plain ca_cert present ⇒ SASL_SSL (that CA); tls: true ⇒ SASL_SSL (system/public roots); neither ⇒ SASL_PLAINTEXT kafka-mtls.yaml mtls client cert + key (client is authenticated) kafka-unauthenticated-tls.yaml unauthenticated_tls one-way TLS; client not authenticated kafka-unauthenticated-plaintext.yaml unauthenticated_plaintext no auth, no TLS; test/lab only

ca_cert (on sasl_scram, sasl_plain, mtls, unauthenticated_tls) is the PEM path used to verify the broker's TLS certificate, and is honoured on both the source read and the cluster-link truststore. Supply it only for a private/internal CA; public-CA brokers (AWS MSK, Confluent Cloud) validate against the system trust store and need no ca_cert. For sasl_plain on a public-CA listener, set tls: true (with no ca_cert) to select SASL_SSL over the system trust store — otherwise sasl_plain without either signal is SASL_PLAINTEXT (cleartext).

This is not the kcp scan apache-kafka-credentials.yaml format. The scan format lists multiple clusters:, each with its own bootstrap_servers, an auth_method: wrapper with use: flags, and scan-only metrics blocks. Passing the scan format to a migrate credentials file is rejected with a hint.

docs.title: REST credentials
docs.text:
Authenticate to the Kafka Admin / Cluster Links REST API. Specify exactly one block (or the api_key/api_secret pair).

File Method Notes rest-api-key.yaml api_key + api_secret Confluent Cloud; top-level pair; public CA rest-basic.yaml basic username/password (e.g. CP MDS) rest-bearer.yaml bearer token (e.g. MDS/OAuth) rest-mtls.yaml mtls client cert + key; auth at the TLS layer

basic, bearer, and mtls each accept an optional ca_cert and insecure_skip_verify to reach a TLS endpoint fronted by a private/internal CA (e.g. self-managed CP / MDS). Public-CA endpoints (Confluent Cloud via api_key) need neither.

docs.title: Connection Settings in the Migration Manifest
docs.text: Four sections of the migration manifest tell kcp where your source and destination Apache Kafka® clusters, the cluster link, and Confluent Gateway are: spec.source, spec.target, spec.clusterLink, and spec.gateway.

docs.title: spec.source
docs.text:
The cluster being migrated from. kcp only ever reads from it.

Field Type Required Notes type enum yes msk or apache-kafka. Gates auth: iam is valid only for msk. bootstrapServers []string yes Non-empty. Each entry is host:port. credentials path yes Path to a Kafka-family credentials file. See Credentials in the Migration Manifest.

confluent-platform is not a valid value here. This manifest only ever points at a link that already exists, so it never needs to act as a source-side link initiator.

docs.title: spec.target
docs.text:
The cluster being migrated to.

Field Type Required Notes type enum yes confluent-cloud or confluent-platform. clusterId string yes Required for both destination types: this kind never discovers it live. kafka.bootstrapServers []string yes Destination Kafka bootstrap. kafka.restEndpoint string yes Destination Admin REST endpoint (cluster link + topic operations). kafka.clusterCredentials path yes Path to the destination Kafka leg credentials file, dialed directly to read destination-side offsets. Accepts sasl_plain, sasl_scram, mtls, unauthenticated_tls, or unauthenticated_plaintext (see below).

The destination REST (cluster-link) credential is not on spec.target.kafka. It lives separately at spec.clusterLink.linkCredentials and is always required.

kafka.clusterCredentials accepts any Kafka auth method except iam. The destination is Confluent Cloud or Confluent Platform, never MSK, so iam is rejected rather than silently accepted and then failing opaquely at connection time. The rejection happens when execute (including --dry-run) reads the credentials file, not when the manifest is parsed. lag-check never reads that file. As on the source leg, a ca_cert inside sasl_plain names a private CA the client trusts directly, on top of (or instead of) the public truststore tls: true selects.

Unlike a source sasl_plain, a destination sasl_plain with neither ca_cert nor tls set does not fall back to SASL_PLAINTEXT: it defaults to tls: true against the public truststore. The destination is always a managed or production cluster, never on-premises plaintext like a source might legitimately be. No sasl_plain field opts back into SASL_PLAINTEXT against the destination. For a genuinely plaintext destination (test or lab only), use unauthenticated_plaintext.

docs.title: spec.clusterLink
docs.text:
Field Type Required Default Notes name string yes — Name of a cluster link that already exists on the destination. This kind never creates one. bootstrapServers []string no — Repeats spec.target.kafka.bootstrapServers for manifest self-documentation. Not validated against it. linkCredentials path yes — Path to the destination REST (cluster-link) credentials file. See REST credentials.

spec.clusterLink takes a single link, and a dynamic route is paired with one link: the same link for every topic-based migration batch on the route and for the route conversion, which takes its scope (the topics and consumer groups to move) from it. kcp doesn't check that separate manifests for the same route name the same link, so don't split one route's batches across links.

Why two destination credentials at all? spec.target.kafka.clusterCredentials authenticates a direct Kafka-protocol connection to the destination bootstrapServers. spec.clusterLink.linkCredentials authenticates HTTP calls to restEndpoint's Admin REST API, which is what actually manages the cluster link (status, list and promote mirror topics, alter configurations). These are two different servers speaking two different protocols. On self-managed Confluent Platform they are backed by two independent credential stores the operator configures separately on the cluster: the Kafka SASL/SCRAM (or mTLS) listener has its own store, while the REST API's auth, set by kafka.rest.authentication.method, has another: a Basic realm file, Metadata Service (MDS) for bearer, or its own mTLS truststore. A valid Kafka credential is not automatically a valid REST credential, even against the same broker process. linkCredentials is therefore always required and never derived from the Kafka leg. Its top-level shape is one of an api_key and api_secret pair, basic, bearer, or mtls (see the REST credentials table).

docs.title: spec.gateway
docs.text:
The manifest has no crs.fenced or crs.switchover file: kcp derives both the fenced custom resource (CR) and the switched CR from the live initial CR at cutover. On a static route that is a route-level fence added to the route named in the declared section's route, then that route's streamingDomain flipped to its declared target. On a dynamic route it is a rules.fencing entry for the selected topics, then a routing condition sending those topics to the target domain. The old crs.initial nesting is flattened to a single cr-name, and the retired crs and routes keys are removed from the schema entirely: a stale manifest that still uses them fails the strict decode with an unknown-field error.

Field Type Required Notes namespace string yes Kubernetes namespace where the Gateway is deployed. kubeconfig string no Path to the kubeconfig to use. The one field in this manifest where a leading ~/ is expanded. If unset, kcp uses the pod's in-cluster service account when it runs in a pod, and ~/.kube/config otherwise. cr-name string yes The name of the initial Gateway CR, read live from the cluster on each execute run. Not a file path.

docs.title: Credentials in the Migration Manifest
docs.text:
Every credentials-shaped slot (spec.source.credentials, spec.target.kafka.clusterCredentials, spec.clusterLink.linkCredentials) is a path to an external credentials file. Inline credential blocks are not accepted, so the manifest itself never holds secret material:

credentials: /etc/kcp/source-creds.yaml

The referenced file's top-level content is the credential: for the Apache Kafka® legs, a Kafka-family block, and for linkCredentials, a REST block. Prefer a credential mounted as a Kubernetes Secret file. Each credentials file is secret-bearing. If one is group- or world-readable, kcp warns rather than fails, so keep it 0600.

docs.title: Kafka credentials (spec.source.credentials, spec.target.kafka.clusterCredentials)
docs.text:
Specify exactly one method block. Its presence selects it (no auth_method: wrapper, no use: flag). An optional top-level insecure_skip_tls_verify: false sibling applies to test environments only, and takes effect only where a TLS handshake happens (not for unauthenticated_plaintext or sasl_plain over plaintext). REST credentials use a different key, insecure_skip_verify, inside their block.

Method Required fields Notes iam region MSK source only. Confluent Cloud can't present IAM (a link to MSK uses SCRAM instead). sasl_scram username, password, mechanism mechanism is SHA256 or SHA512 and must be set: an omitted mechanism is rejected. SCRAM-SHA-256 and SCRAM-SHA-512 are accepted too. MSK requires SHA512. Optional ca_cert. Always TLS (SASL_SSL). sasl_plain username, password Optional ca_cert, tls. ca_cert present ⇒ SASL_SSL against that CA. tls: true ⇒ SASL_SSL over the system (public) truststore. Neither ⇒ SASL_PLAINTEXT on the source leg (the destination leg always uses TLS, as described in spec.target). mtls client_cert, client_key Optional ca_cert. The client is authenticated by its certificate. unauthenticated_tls — Optional ca_cert. One-way TLS. The client is not authenticated. unauthenticated_plaintext — Write it as unauthenticated_plaintext: {}. A block is selected by its presence, so a bare key with no value is rejected. No auth, no TLS. Test or lab only.

ca_cert (on sasl_scram, sasl_plain, mtls, unauthenticated_tls) is a PEM file path used to verify the broker's TLS certificate. Supply it only for a private or internal CA. Public-CA brokers (AWS MSK, Confluent Cloud) validate against the system truststore and need no ca_cert. Every ca_cert, client_cert, and client_key path must exist when the credentials file is read.

Each of the following examples is the complete contents of a credentials file.

SASL/SCRAM (for example, an MSK source):

sasl_scram:
  username: kcp-migration
  password: <password>
  mechanism: SHA512

mTLS, with a private CA:

mtls:
  client_cert: /etc/kcp/certs/client.crt
  client_key: /etc/kcp/certs/client.key
  ca_cert: /etc/kcp/certs/ca.crt

IAM (MSK source only):

iam:
  region: us-east-1

docs.title: REST credentials (spec.clusterLink.linkCredentials)
docs.text:
Specify exactly one block (or the api_key and api_secret pair).

Method Required fields Notes api_key + api_secret api_key, api_secret Confluent Cloud. Flat top-level pair. Public CA. basic username, password For example, Confluent Platform Metadata Service (MDS). bearer token For example, MDS or OAuth. mtls client_cert, client_key Auth at the TLS layer.

basic, bearer, and mtls each accept an optional ca_cert and insecure_skip_verify inside their block to reach a TLS endpoint fronted by a private or internal CA (for example, MDS on a self-managed Confluent Platform). The flat api_key form takes the same two keys at the top level instead, and they are rejected alongside the block forms. Public-CA endpoints (Confluent Cloud) need neither. basic does not check at load time that username and password are non-empty. A missing value surfaces as an authentication error at runtime.

Each of the following examples is the complete contents of a credentials file.

Confluent Cloud (api_key + api_secret):

api_key: <api_key>
api_secret: <api_secret>

Self-managed Confluent Platform, with a private CA (basic):

basic:
  username: kcp-migration
  password: <password>
  ca_cert: /etc/kcp/certs/ca.crt

One restriction is specific to this manifest, narrower than the two tables above: spec.source.credentials.iam is valid only when spec.source.type: msk, and spec.target.kafka.clusterCredentials.iam is rejected outright, because the destination is Confluent Cloud or Confluent Platform, never MSK.

docs.title: Example Cutover Manifests
docs.text: This page has one fully annotated, ready-to-copy manifest per migration type, with comments on every field. Each is also available as a plain file under gateway-examples/. Each file link downloads the raw file rather than opening it in the browser.

docs.title: Static migration
docs.text:
gateway-static-migration.yaml

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confluentinc/kcp/main/internal/manifest/gatewaymigration.schema.json
#
# A STATIC migration (all-at-once, AAO): every selected topic cuts over together
# across a STATIC Gateway route.
#
#   kcp migration cutover execute --migration-yaml gateway-static-migration.yaml
#   kcp migration cutover lag-check --migration-yaml gateway-static-migration.yaml
#
# The migration type is declared by which section of spec is present: exactly one
# of staticMigration, dynamicMigration or dynamicToStaticConversion. kcp checks
# the declaration against the live Gateway CR and refuses to run if the route's
# mode disagrees (a staticMigration needs a static route).
#
# Paths in this file resolve relative to the PROCESS working directory, not to
# the file's own location. The one exception is spec.gateway.kubeconfig, where a
# leading ~/ is expanded.
#
# Every credentials field is a PATH to a credentials file — inline secret blocks
# are not accepted — so this manifest carries no secret material itself. Keep the
# referenced credentials files 0600.

apiVersion: kcp.confluent.io/v1alpha1
kind: GatewayMigration

metadata:
  # The migration identity, used as its migration_id label in logs and output.
  name: msk-prod-to-cc-batch-1

spec:
  # kcp only ever READS from the source.
  source:
    type: msk # msk | apache-kafka. Gates auth: iam is msk-only.
    bootstrapServers:
      - b-1.msk-prod.abc123.c2.kafka.us-east-1.amazonaws.com:9096
      - b-2.msk-prod.abc123.c2.kafka.us-east-1.amazonaws.com:9096
    # Path to the source Kafka credentials file (auth only). Its top-level shape
    # for MSK, e.g.:
    #   sasl_scram: { username: ..., password: ..., mechanism: SHA512 }
    # (MSK is SHA512-only; iam is also valid for an MSK source.)
    credentials: /etc/kcp/source-creds.yaml

  target:
    type: confluent-cloud # confluent-cloud | confluent-platform
    clusterId: lkc-abc123 # required for BOTH destination types
    kafka:
      bootstrapServers:
        - pkc-xxxxx.us-east-1.aws.confluent.cloud:9092
      restEndpoint: https://pkc-xxxxx.us-east-1.aws.confluent.cloud:443
      # Path to the destination KAFKA credentials file — the leg dialled directly
      # to bootstrapServers to read destination-side offsets. Its top-level shape
      # accepts sasl_plain, sasl_scram, mtls, unauthenticated_tls, or
      # unauthenticated_plaintext — iam is rejected (the destination is Confluent
      # Cloud/Platform, never MSK). Examples:
      #   sasl_plain: { username: ..., password: ..., tls: true }   # Confluent Cloud
      #   sasl_scram: { username: ..., password: ..., mechanism: SHA256, ca_cert: ... }
      #   mtls:       { client_cert: ..., client_key: ..., ca_cert: ... }
      clusterCredentials: /etc/kcp/dest-kafka-creds.yaml

  clusterLink:
    name: msk-to-cc # the link must ALREADY EXIST on the destination
    # Repeats spec.target.kafka.bootstrapServers, for self-documentation.
    bootstrapServers:
      - pkc-xxxxx.us-east-1.aws.confluent.cloud:9092
    # Path to the cluster-link REST credentials file — the credential that calls
    # restEndpoint's Admin REST API, which is what actually manages the cluster
    # link (status, list/promote mirror topics, alter configs). Always required;
    # never derived. Its top-level shape is one of: api_key/api_secret, basic,
    # bearer, or mtls. Examples:
    #   api_key: ...            # + api_secret: ...   (Confluent Cloud)
    #   basic:  { username: ..., password: ... }      (CP Basic realm)
    #   bearer: { token: ... }                        (MDS/RBAC)
    #   mtls:   { client_cert: ..., client_key: ... }
    linkCredentials: /etc/kcp/link-creds.yaml

  gateway:
    namespace: confluent
    # kubeconfig: ~/.kube/config          # optional (unset: in-cluster in a pod, else ~/.kube/config); a leading ~/ IS expanded
    cr-name: gateway-initial # a Kubernetes object NAME, read live

  staticMigration:
    # route names the route to fence/switch and the streaming domain it switches
    # to. kcp reads the live initial CR, injects fence: {scope: ALL, errorCode:
    # BROKER_NOT_AVAILABLE} onto the named route, and applies the patched CR —
    # there is no separate fenced-CR file. At cutover kcp derives the switched CR
    # the same way, flipping the route's streamingDomain to the target declared
    # here. This is safe with NO secret or auth change at cutover only because
    # the route's security.cluster already carries pre-staged ("redundant") swap
    # auth for the target domain; kcp checks that staging on every run, before
    # anything is fenced.
    route:
      name: migration-route # a pre-existing STATIC route in the initial CR
      targetStreamingDomain: confluent-cloud

    # topicGroup pairs the topic selection that migrates. Exactly one entry.
    #
    # topics is a flat list of LITERAL topic names — not globs. topicPatterns is
    # a list of anchored full-match regular expressions (RE2), matched against the
    # topic names on the source cluster. At least one of the two is REQUIRED; both
    # may be set (their union is used). Every selected topic must be a mirror
    # topic on the cluster link, or the run is refused. To cut over EVERY source
    # topic, use the match-all pattern: topicPatterns: ['.*'].
    #
    # Note the selection has NO effect on `lag-check`, which always watches every
    # mirror.
    topicGroup:
      - topics: ['t1.order', 't1.inventory', 't2.order']
        # topicPatterns: ['orders\..*']

    # OPTIONAL. Disable the link's consumer.offset.sync.enable right after the
    # fence, and set it back to `baseline` after the switch. A run that stops
    # before that restore leaves it owed, and re-running execute performs it.
    consumerOffsetSync:
      pause: true
      # The state consumer.offset.sync.enable was in BEFORE this migration
      # started ("enabled" or "disabled"). Required when pause is set, since a
      # resumed run cannot observe the pre-migration value itself.
      baseline: enabled

    # OPTIONAL, and read FRESH on every execute, so a change takes effect on the
    # next run. Each value is a DEFAULT: `kcp migration cutover execute` can override any
    # of them for a single run with the matching flag (e.g.
    # --detect-unrouted-producers-duration 60s), no edit needed.
    policies:
      lagThreshold: 0
      promoteBatchSize: 100 # 0 = promote all at once
      rolloutTimeout: 10m # 0 = no deadline
      detectUnroutedProducersDuration: 30s # 0 = CHECK SKIPPED; min 10s when set
      consumerOffsetSyncDrainDuration: 15s # 0 = no wait; needs consumerOffsetSync.pause
      hotReloadTimeout: 90s # 0 = built-in 90s budget; never unbounded
      gatewayConfigPort: 0 # 0 = the gateway default (9180)

docs.title: Dynamic migration
docs.text:
gateway-dynamic-migration.yaml

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confluentinc/kcp/main/internal/manifest/gatewaymigration.schema.json
#
# A DYNAMIC migration (topic-based, TBM): topics cut over incrementally across a
# DYNAMIC Gateway route, promoting mirror topics at zero lag. Run one manifest
# per batch of topics; each batch's topicGroup selects only that batch.
#
#   kcp migration cutover execute --migration-yaml gateway-dynamic-migration.yaml
#
# Everything outside spec.dynamicMigration is identical to
# gateway-static-migration.yaml, which documents every shared field. The
# migration type is the section declared; kcp refuses to run if the live route
# is not dynamic. There is no consumerOffsetSync block: it is static-only.

apiVersion: kcp.confluent.io/v1alpha1
kind: GatewayMigration

metadata:
  name: msk-prod-to-cc-tbm-batch-1

spec:
  source:
    type: msk
    bootstrapServers:
      - b-1.msk-prod.abc123.c2.kafka.us-east-1.amazonaws.com:9096
      - b-2.msk-prod.abc123.c2.kafka.us-east-1.amazonaws.com:9096
    credentials: /etc/kcp/source-creds.yaml

  target:
    type: confluent-cloud
    clusterId: lkc-abc123
    kafka:
      bootstrapServers:
        - pkc-xxxxx.us-east-1.aws.confluent.cloud:9092
      restEndpoint: https://pkc-xxxxx.us-east-1.aws.confluent.cloud:443
      clusterCredentials: /etc/kcp/dest-kafka-creds.yaml

  clusterLink:
    name: msk-to-cc
    bootstrapServers:
      - pkc-xxxxx.us-east-1.aws.confluent.cloud:9092
    linkCredentials: /etc/kcp/link-creds.yaml

  gateway:
    namespace: confluent
    cr-name: gateway-initial

  dynamicMigration:
    route:
      name: migration-route # a pre-existing DYNAMIC route in the initial CR
      targetStreamingDomain: confluent-cloud

    # This batch only. Later batches are separate manifests with disjoint topics.
    topicGroup:
      - topics: ['t1.order', 't1.inventory']

    policies:
      lagThreshold: 0
      promoteBatchSize: 100 # 0 = promote all at once
      rolloutTimeout: 10m # 0 = no deadline
      detectUnroutedProducersDuration: 30s # 0 = CHECK SKIPPED; min 10s when set
      hotReloadTimeout: 90s
      gatewayConfigPort: 0

docs.title: Route conversion
docs.text:
A route conversion declares spec.dynamicToStaticConversion in place of a migration section (see Route Conversion Settings in the Migration Manifest). gateway-route-conversion.yaml

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/confluentinc/kcp/main/internal/manifest/gatewaymigration.schema.json
#
# A DYNAMIC-TO-STATIC route conversion (d2s): once a topic-based migration has
# migrated every topic on its cluster link, convert the dynamic route to a static
# route bound to the destination, carrying the consumer groups' committed offsets
# across. Topics stay the same; the route's mode changes.
#
#   kcp migration cutover execute --migration-yaml gateway-route-conversion.yaml --dry-run
#   kcp migration cutover execute --migration-yaml gateway-route-conversion.yaml
#
# The topology, auth and credentials files are the topic-based migration's own;
# gateway-static-migration.yaml documents every shared field. Paths in this file
# resolve relative to the PROCESS working directory.

apiVersion: kcp.confluent.io/v1alpha1
kind: GatewayMigration

metadata:
  name: msk-prod-to-cc-convert

spec:
  source:
    type: msk
    bootstrapServers:
      - b-1.msk-prod.abc123.c2.kafka.us-east-1.amazonaws.com:9096
      - b-2.msk-prod.abc123.c2.kafka.us-east-1.amazonaws.com:9096
    # Must be able to list every consumer group and describe every topic.
    credentials: /etc/kcp/source-creds.yaml

  target:
    type: confluent-cloud
    clusterId: lkc-abc123
    kafka:
      bootstrapServers:
        - pkc-xxxxx.us-east-1.aws.confluent.cloud:9092
      restEndpoint: https://pkc-xxxxx.us-east-1.aws.confluent.cloud:443
      # Must also be able to list every consumer group, describe every topic and
      # write consumer-group offsets (READ on the groups and the topics): the
      # conversion copies the source's committed offsets here.
      clusterCredentials: /etc/kcp/dest-kafka-creds.yaml

  clusterLink:
    # The link the topic-based migration used. Every mirror topic on it is in
    # scope, and every one must be promoted.
    name: msk-to-cc
    linkCredentials: /etc/kcp/link-creds.yaml

  gateway:
    namespace: confluent
    cr-name: gateway-initial

  dynamicToStaticConversion:
    route:
      name: migration-route # the dynamic route the topic-based migration used
      # One of the two domains the dynamic route binds. Its binding's
      # bootstrapServerId is what the static route binds to.
      targetStreamingDomain: confluent-cloud
    # No topicGroup: a conversion covers every mirror on the link.

    policies:
      # The wait between the two committed-offset snapshots taken after the
      # fence, to catch a consumer committing to the source directly. Every topic
      # on the route is blocked for at least this long. 0s = skip the check;
      # min 10s when set.
      detectUnroutedCommitsDuration: 30s
      offsetSyncConcurrency: 0 # workers reading and writing offsets; 0 = built-in 8
      rolloutTimeout: 10m # 0 = no deadline
      hotReloadTimeout: 90s # 0 = built-in 90s budget; never unbounded

docs.title: Migration Sections in the Migration Manifest
docs.text: Each of spec.staticMigration, spec.dynamicMigration, and spec.dynamicToStaticConversion names the route to fence and switch over and the target streaming domain it switches to. The two migrations also carry the topic selection. <section> below stands for whichever one the manifest declares.

docs.title: spec.<section>.route
docs.text: Field Type Required Notes name string yes A spec.routes[].name in the initial Gateway custom resource (CR) to fence and switch over. Must be non-blank (checked when the manifest is read) and exist in the CR (checked at reconcile). targetStreamingDomain string yes The streaming domain this route switches to. On a static route it must be declared in the initial CR's spec.streamingDomains with exactly one bootstrap server ID, and the route must already carry pre-staged security.cluster.<domain> auth for it (a secretStore and an authentication block, with the referenced Secrets present). On a dynamic route it must be one of the two domains the route binds. For a conversion (dynamicToStaticConversion) it must be one of the two domains the dynamic route binds, and that binding must carry a bootstrapServerId: the static route binds to it.

docs.title: spec.<staticMigration|dynamicMigration>.topicGroup
docs.text:
Required for both migrations. A dynamicToStaticConversion has none (the cluster link is its scope). A list validated to exactly one entry (one route, one migration per file).

Field Type Required Notes topics []string see note A flat list of literal topic names, not globs. A glob is not rejected when the manifest is read. It fails at reconcile as "not found on the source". topicPatterns []string see note A list of anchored full-match regular expressions (RE2), matched against the topic names on the source cluster. Case-sensitive, and the whole topic name must match. . matches any character, so escape it (\.) to match a literal dot. ['.*'] selects every source topic.

At least one of topics or topicPatterns is required. When both are set, the union is migrated: every literal name plus every source topic a pattern matches. Every selected topic must be in a state kcp can migrate or resume: a topic that is not on the source, not on the cluster link, present on the destination without being a mirror, or whose mirror is in a failed or unexpected state refuses the run, while a topic an earlier run already promoted or switched is resumed or skipped. The refusal is all-or-nothing: nothing is fenced or changed. If nothing is left to migrate, execute reports that and does nothing. Omitting topics does not select every topic: to migrate every source topic, write an explicit match-all pattern, topicPatterns: ['.*'].

topicPatterns are resolved against the live source on every run, so the selected set can change between runs without the manifest changing. On a dynamic route, that matters when you resume an interrupted migration (see Execution model).

The route's mode is not declared separately: the section you declare fixes the mode the route must have, and kcp reads the live CR on every execute run to check it. It uses the route's own mode field when the CR sets one. Otherwise, it infers the mode from the binding: a named singular streamingDomain ⇒ static, a non-empty plural streamingDomains ⇒ dynamic. A route with both or neither is refused, as is a route whose mode disagrees with the declared section. On a static route, the bootstrap server ID is derived from the target domain's declaration in the live CR, not written in the manifest. kcp migration cutover execute runs the workflow that matches the declared type: a whole-route cutover for staticMigration, topic by topic for dynamicMigration.

A dynamic route has two further requirements, both checked at reconcile (so --dry-run reports them): it must bind exactly two streaming domains (the source and the target), with coordination.group pinned to the source domain, and the cluster link's consumer offset sync must already be disabled, which is why spec.dynamicMigration has no consumerOffsetSync section.

lag-check ignores the topic selection entirely and always watches every mirror topic.

docs.title: spec.staticMigration.consumerOffsetSync
docs.text:
Optional, static migrations only.

Field Type Required Default Notes pause bool no false Disable the link's consumer.offset.sync.enable right after fencing, and set it back to baseline after the switch. If a run stops before that restore, the restore is still owed and re-running execute performs it. It is also restored if a failure before promote rolls the fence back. baseline string when pausing — enabled or disabled: the value consumer.offset.sync.enable is set back to after the switch.

docs.title: Cutover Migration Manifest Reference
docs.text:
kcp migration cutover execute runs a cutover described by a single YAML manifest, gateway-static-migration.yaml, gateway-dynamic-migration.yaml, or gateway-route-conversion.yaml: it fences the route in Confluent Gateway, promotes the mirror topics on the cluster link in batches, and switches production traffic over to the destination.

The manifest declares which of three workflows it runs: all at once on a static route (spec.staticMigration), topic by topic on a dynamic route (spec.dynamicMigration), or a conversion of a dynamic route to static (spec.dynamicToStaticConversion) after every topic on the cluster link is migrated. kcp migration cutover lag-check reads the same manifest to show replication lag on the cluster link.

Page What it covers Run a Migration Cutover How execute resumes and what to know before you run it Connection Settings in the Migration Manifest spec.source, spec.target, spec.clusterLink, spec.gateway Migration Sections in the Migration Manifest route, topicGroup, and consumerOffsetSync for static and dynamic migrations Route Conversion Settings in the Migration Manifest spec.dynamicToStaticConversion Policies in the Migration Manifest Per-run defaults and their override flags Credentials in the Migration Manifest Apache Kafka® and REST credentials files Migration Manifest Validation and Field Reference Validation rules and every field in one table Example Cutover Manifests One annotated manifest per migration type

docs.title: Declare the migration type
docs.text:
A GatewayMigration manifest declares what it does by which one section of spec it carries. Exactly one is required:

Section What it does Live route must be Example staticMigration Migrates topics together across a static route (all-at-once). static gateway-static-migration.yaml dynamicMigration Migrates topics in batches across a dynamic route (topic-based). dynamic gateway-dynamic-migration.yaml dynamicToStaticConversion Converts a fully-migrated dynamic route to a static route. Topics stay the same. The route's mode changes. dynamic gateway-route-conversion.yaml

A migration moves topic ownership from the source to the destination and leaves the route's mode unchanged. A conversion changes the route's mode and leaves the topics unchanged, so it selects no topics. kcp compares your declaration with the live Gateway custom resource (CR) and refuses to run if the route's mode disagrees. Each section carries its own route, its own policies (only the fields that type uses), and, for migrations, a topicGroup. A policy flag (such as --promote-batch-size) that the declared type does not have is an error.

If you are upgrading a manifest from an earlier build: spec.route and spec.defaultPolicies were replaced by the sections above, and spec.clusterLink.pauseConsumerOffsetSync and consumerOffsetSyncBaseline moved to spec.staticMigration.consumerOffsetSync.pause and .baseline, respectively.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
apiVersion: kcp.confluent.io/v1alpha1 # required, exact literal
kind: GatewayMigration # required, exact literal
metadata:
  name: my-migration # required, non-blank — the migration identity
spec:
  source: { ... } # required — cluster being migrated from
  target: { ... } # required — cluster being migrated to
  clusterLink: { ... } # required — an ALREADY-EXISTING cluster link
  gateway: { ... } # required — namespace, kubeconfig, initial gateway CR name
  # Exactly one of the next three — the declared migration type:
  staticMigration: { ... } # route, topicGroup, consumerOffsetSync, policies
  dynamicMigration: { ... } # route, topicGroup, policies
  dynamicToStaticConversion: { ... } # route, policies (no topicGroup)

apiVersion must equal kcp.confluent.io/v1alpha1 and kind must equal GatewayMigration, exactly. metadata.name is required and non-blank: it is the migration's identity, used as its migration_id in logs and output. spec.source, spec.target, spec.clusterLink, and spec.gateway are always required, as is exactly one of spec.staticMigration, spec.dynamicMigration, and spec.dynamicToStaticConversion. Each section's policies is optional.

Every credentials field is a path to a credentials file. The manifest never holds secret material inline, and kcp does not substitute ${ENV_VAR} references: a ${VAR}-shaped value is read literally.

docs.title: Commands that read the manifest
docs.text:
Command Flag Required Notes kcp migration cutover execute --migration-yaml yes Path to this manifest. --dry-run no Run only the reconcile step and print the plan, changing nothing. Exits non-zero if the plan is refused. --lag-threshold, --promote-batch-size, --rollout-timeout, --detect-unrouted-producers-duration, --consumer-offset-sync-drain-duration, --hot-reload-timeout, --gateway-config-port, --detect-unrouted-commits-duration, --offset-sync-concurrency no Per-run overrides of the matching field in the declared section's policies, for this run only. A flag the declared type does not have is an error, including under --dry-run. kcp migration cutover lag-check --migration-yaml yes Path to this manifest. Reads only the destination REST leg (spec.clusterLink.linkCredentials), honored in whichever form it resolves (api_key, basic, bearer, or mtls). It never dials the source or destination Kafka legs. --poll-interval no (default 1) Poll interval in seconds. Values outside 1-60 are clamped to that range.

Every path in the manifest resolves relative to the process working directory, not the manifest's own location. The one exception is spec.gateway.kubeconfig, where a leading ~/ is expanded. The same applies to the certificate and key paths inside a credentials file.

Every flag can also be set through an uppercase environment variable of the same name with dashes as underscores (--lag-threshold is LAG_THRESHOLD, --dry-run is DRY_RUN, --poll-interval is POLL_INTERVAL). An explicit flag wins. A policy value set through an environment variable overrides the manifest exactly as the flag would (and an inapplicable one is rejected the same way), so a stray LAG_THRESHOLD in the shell silently changes a run. The overrides are validated with the rest of the effective policy, including under --dry-run.

docs.title: Editor support
docs.text: Each file under gateway-examples/ carries a # yaml-language-server: $schema=… modeline that fetches the manifest's JSON schema from the main branch of the kcp repository on GitHub (internal/manifest/gatewaymigration.schema.json), so VS Code with the Red Hat YAML extension gives autocomplete and inline validation when it can reach GitHub. The schema covers structure and types but does not enforce every rule (for example, it does not check the 10s minimum or the host:port format), so kcp migration cutover execute --dry-run is the authoritative check.

docs.title: Policies in the Migration Manifest
docs.text:
Each declared section of the migration manifest has its own optional policies block, and every field in it is a default that a matching kcp migration cutover execute flag can override for a single run. The block is re-read fresh from the manifest on every execute, never fixed once.

A field a section does not have is rejected by the strict decode, and a policy flag the declared type does not have is an error (it names the flag and the section). Duration values need a unit, such as 0s, 90s, or 10m. In the manifest, a bare number such as 0 or 90 is a parse error (the command-line flags do accept a plain 0). Negative values are rejected.

Field staticMigration dynamicMigration dynamicToStaticConversion lagThreshold yes yes — promoteBatchSize yes yes — rolloutTimeout yes yes yes detectUnroutedProducersDuration yes yes — consumerOffsetSyncDrainDuration yes — — detectUnroutedCommitsDuration — — yes offsetSyncConcurrency — — yes hotReloadTimeout yes yes yes gatewayConfigPort yes yes yes Field Type Default Override flag Notes lagThreshold int 0 --lag-threshold Replication lag tolerated per topic: each selected topic's lag (the sum of its partition lags) must be at or below this before the run fences. 0 is the strictest (fully caught up). promoteBatchSize int 0 --promote-batch-size Max mirror topics promoted per batch. 0 promotes all at once. When set, each batch is promoted and confirmed stopped before the next is submitted. rolloutTimeout duration 0s --rollout-timeout Max wait, during fence and switchover, for the operator to accept the change and for Confluent Gateway to roll out (for example, 10m). It also bounds the per-pod configuration wait after a pod roll is observed. 0s means no deadline: kcp waits until convergence or cancellation. detectUnroutedProducersDuration duration 0s --detect-unrouted-producers-duration After fencing, kcp takes two source-offset snapshots this far apart to catch producers still bypassing the Gateway. If any partition's offset advanced, the run stops before promote. 0s (the default) skips the check entirely. When set, the minimum is 10s, because a shorter window can't span a producer's metadata refresh. Not available on a conversion, which uses detectUnroutedCommitsDuration instead. consumerOffsetSyncDrainDuration duration 0s --consumer-offset-sync-drain-duration staticMigration only. Wait after fencing, before disabling the link's consumer offset sync, letting final offsets propagate. Has no effect unless consumerOffsetSync.pause is set. 0s means no wait. hotReloadTimeout duration 0s --hot-reload-timeout Max wait for every Gateway pod to report the new configuration revision when the Gateway supports hot-reload (for example, 90s). Unlike rolloutTimeout, this is never unbounded: a hot-reload moves no Kubernetes signal, so 0s uses the built-in 90-second budget rather than waiting forever. gatewayConfigPort int 0 --gateway-config-port Port serving the Gateway's /config endpoint, polled per pod to confirm a configuration revision was applied. 0 uses the Gateway default (9180). detectUnroutedCommitsDuration duration 0s --detect-unrouted-commits-duration dynamicToStaticConversion only. Window between the two committed-offset snapshots taken after fencing, to catch a consumer committing to the source directly, bypassing the Gateway. 0s skips the check. When set, the minimum is 10s. offsetSyncConcurrency int 0 --offset-sync-concurrency dynamicToStaticConversion only. Number of workers, each with its own broker connection, reading and writing consumer-group offsets. 0 uses the built-in 8.

docs.title: Route Conversion Settings in the Migration Manifest
docs.text:
The spec.dynamicToStaticConversion section of the migration manifest replaces the dynamic route that a topic-based migration leaves behind with a static route bound to the destination, and copies the consumer groups' committed offsets there, so group coordination moves too. Run it after every topic on the cluster link is migrated and the last batch has switched.

A topic-based migration leaves its route dynamic: each migrated topic is routed to the destination by a routing condition, and consumer-group coordination stays pinned to the source.

spec:
  dynamicToStaticConversion:
    route:
      name: migration-route
      targetStreamingDomain: confluent-cloud

A conversion selects no topics: the cluster link is its scope. The rest of the manifest (source, target, clusterLink, gateway) is the topic-based migration's. See the conversion example.

docs.title: Conversion checks
docs.text:
execute and --dry-run check the following against the live Gateway custom resource (CR), both clusters, and the cluster link:

  • The route. It is dynamic and binds exactly two streaming domains, with coordination.group on the source. targetStreamingDomain is one of them, and its binding carries a bootstrapServerId. The route carries security.cluster.<targetStreamingDomain> auth. It has no fence kcp didn't write and no route-level fence. The cluster link's consumer offset sync is disabled.
  • The cluster link is the scope. A route pairs with one link, so the link must be the one every batch on the route used: topics migrated over another link are outside the scope, and a group that commits on one refuses the conversion. Every mirror topic on the link must be promoted (STOPPED), named as on the source (no cluster.link.prefix), present on the destination with the same partition count as on the source, and routed to the destination by the dynamic route. At least one topic must be promoted.
  • Consumer groups. A source group whose committed offsets are all on link topics is in scope, and its offsets are copied. A group with any committed offset on a topic that is not on the link refuses the conversion: after the switch that topic is not reachable through the route, or the group belongs to a client outside it. An in-scope group with live members on the destination refuses too. An in-scope group that exists there with no members gets a warning, because kcp overwrites its offsets. Source topics that are not on the link and that no group commits on get a warning: after the switch the route sends their traffic to the destination.
  • Credentials. The source and destination credentials must be able to list every consumer group and describe every topic (a credential that sees part of a cluster would hide a group or a topic from these checks), and the destination credential must be able to write consumer-group offsets (READ on the groups and the topics). On an MSK IAM source, listing every group and describing every topic need the kafka-cluster:DescribeGroup and kafka-cluster:DescribeTopic actions on every group and topic resource.

Keep the cluster link and the source topics until the conversion has run. The link's mirror topics are the conversion's only record of which topics were migrated, and kcp works out the in-scope consumer groups from those topics, so a deleted link leaves it nothing to read and the run fails with an error reading the link's mirror topics rather than a purpose-written refusal. Deleting a source topic purges its groups' committed offsets, so kcp has nothing to copy for it.

docs.title: Conversion steps
docs.text:
1. Fence. kcp adds its conversion fence, {topicPatterns: ['.*'], blocked: true}, at the head of the route's rules.fencing, blocking every topic on the route.
  2. Verify. On data read after the fence, kcp re-runs the route checks that decide whether the route can be converted (dynamic, two domains, coordination.group on the source, targetStreamingDomain one of them, consumer offset sync disabled), confirms its own conversion fence is still on the route, and re-runs the credential, cluster-link scope, and consumer-group checks. It does not repeat the checks on the route's contents (the target binding's bootstrapServerId, the security.cluster.<targetStreamingDomain> auth, no fence kcp didn't write, no route-level fence) or the warnings about topics outside the link. Those run before the fence. It then takes two snapshots of every source group's committed offsets, detectUnroutedCommitsDuration apart, but only when it is set (minimum 10s; the default, 0s, skips the check and the first snapshot is the one synced). A change means a client is committing to the source directly, bypassing the Gateway, and the run fails.
  3. Sync offsets. kcp writes the in-scope groups' committed offsets, with their metadata, to the destination. It refuses the whole sync if an offset is past its destination partition's high-water mark.
  4. Switch. kcp replaces the route with a static route bound to targetStreamingDomain, with no rules (so no fence) and no streamingDomains. security and the rest of the route are kept.

The switch is the point of no return. A failure before it removes the fence and leaves the route as it was. Offsets already written to the destination have no effect until the switch. Each Gateway change is confirmed on every Gateway pod, as in a migration.

docs.title: Effect on clients
docs.text:
• A pause. Every topic on the route is blocked from the fence to the switch: about detectUnroutedCommitsDuration (if set) plus two Gateway reloads. Producers retry, so give them a delivery.timeout.ms longer than that. Consumers fetch nothing and can't commit.
  • A rejoin, and possibly a re-read. After the switch, consumers' group coordinator is on the destination. Each consumer's first commit or heartbeat there fails (the destination doesn't know its member), so it rejoins its group and resumes from the copied offset. It might read again what it fetched between the switch and that first failed commit or heartbeat, and what it consumed just before the fence but couldn't commit. The first part is up to one poll (max.poll.records) for a consumer that commits after every batch, and up to the backlog the fence built for a consumer that auto-commits. This is expected at-least-once behavior. Nothing is skipped.
  • KIP-848 consumers. Consumers that use the group protocol from Kafka Improvement Proposal (KIP) 848 (group.protocol=consumer) can't use a dynamic route at all. They work after the route becomes static.

docs.title: Refusals and fixes
docs.text:
Refusal Fix A link topic's mirror is ACTIVE, not promoted Migrate it in a topic-based migration batch, or promote it if nothing uses it. A link topic's promotion is still in progress Wait for it to reach STOPPED, then re-run. The route sends a link topic to the source Finish that topic's batch (re-run execute on its manifest) before converting. A link topic has more partitions on the destination than on the source Add partitions to the source copy to match, set the affected groups' offsets on the new partitions, then re-run. A link topic has fewer partitions on the destination than on the source, or a partition count can't be read Make the destination match the source, or re-run if the read failed. The conversion refuses until the counts agree. A mirror is named differently on the destination Conversions don't support a cluster link with cluster.link.prefix. No topic on the link is promoted Migrate the route's topics first: a conversion closes a topic-based migration. A group commits on a topic that is not on the link Migrate that topic, delete the group's stale offsets on it (kafka-consumer-groups --delete-offsets) or the group itself, or stop or move the application outside this route that owns it. An in-scope group has members on the destination Stop the destination members first. A credential can't list every group, describe every topic, or write offsets Grant what the refusal names, then re-run. The route has a fence kcp didn't write Find out what it is for first. If it is an unfinished topic-based migration batch's, finish that batch (rerun kcp migration cutover execute on its manifest): removing its fence would send producers back to a source topic the link no longer mirrors. Otherwise remove it: the conversion would drop it. The route has a route-level fence Remove it: the static route would enforce it. Committed offsets changed after the fence A client commits to the source directly. Send it through the Gateway, then re-run.

A refusal before the fence changes nothing, and --dry-run shows it.

docs.title: Interruptions
docs.text:
• A killed run leaves the fence up. kcp doesn't clean up when it is stopped (Ctrl+C, SIGTERM, or a crash), so the route keeps blocking every topic until you re-run the same manifest, which resumes.
  • A refusal with the fence up warns. If a re-run is refused while kcp's fence is on the route, kcp says so: the route keeps blocking every topic until you fix the refusal and re-run, or remove kcp's entry from rules.fencing by hand.
  • A failed switch keeps the fence. If the static route never reached the Gateway CR, fix the cause and re-run to finish. If it reached the CR but couldn't be confirmed, check the Gateway (operator acceptance, pods) instead of re-running: a re-run would report nothing to do.
  • A finished conversion re-runs as nothing to do.
